title: The last glimpse of Erin
html_source: Wikipedia says that “Erin” is a Hiberno-English derivative of the Irish word “Éirinn”. “Éirinn” is the dative case of the Irish word for Ireland. “The last glimpse of Erin,” comes from a song by Thomas Moore: “Tho' the last glimpse of Erin with sorrow I see, / Yet wherever thou art shall seem Erin to me; / In exile thy bosom shall bosom shall still be my home.” This is relevant considering Joyce’s self-imposed exile from the land that obsessed him so.
